page: Google Cloud Platform c4d-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is equipped with 126.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 7.88 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate exceptional single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier status in single-core stress-ng CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. For machine learning workloads, the CPU demonstrates strong prompt processing and top-tier text generation speeds for small language models, though performance scales down to average levels for medium-sized models.

From a resource density perspective, the high memory-to-vCPU ratio provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. However, the lack of bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses represents a clear tradeoff, requiring external block storage attachment. This profile is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, small-scale LLM inference, database operations, and general-purpose enterprise workloads requiring strong single-thread execution.

Benchmarks highlight top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, alongside average multi-core and memory bandwidth capabilities. It also delivers strong to top-tier execution speeds for small-scale language model inference. Lacking bundled local storage or public IPv4 addresses, this instance offers a high-memory profile that is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads. It is highly suitable for database operations, memory-intensive applications, and single-thread-heavy enterprise tasks.
